summary: The installed permission rule and its verification set do not cover the controller command surface consistently: the rule text lists only run and status in match, while installation checks refresh and stop, and the reviewed interface also requires review and install-and-run.
steps: Define one canonical list of externally approved controller actions.
Generate the rule match entries from that list.
Verify every approved action against both the candidate and effective policy.
Add negative checks that remain scoped to the intended dedicated rule semantics.
assumptions: The packet does not define the exact semantics of codex execpolicy prefix_rule(match=...). Under the usual restrictive allowlist interpretation, commands absent from match are denied.
The stated interface is authoritative that install-and-run, run, status, refresh, stop, and review are approved entrypoint actions.
Internal actions such as _checks and _builtin must remain unavailable through the installed external rule.
checks: The supplied verification reports 44 passing tests, but the listed tests do not demonstrate that the actual installed rule permits review.
The controller's installation code checks positives for install-and-run, run, status, refresh, and stop, but omits review.
evidence: scripts/run_accounting_master.py: rule_text defines match entries only for run and status.
scripts/run_accounting_master.py: install_rule checks positive commands for install-and-run, run, status, refresh, and stop, but not review.
scripts/run_accounting_master.py: main exposes review as a normal controller action.
tests/test_accounting_master.py: the supplied test-name list contains no test proving that the installed rule allows review.

issues.finding: Permission installation is internally inconsistent and may block required controller operations. rule_text emits match entries only for [python3, run_accounting_master.py, run] and [python3, run_accounting_master.py, status]. The installer nevertheless treats refresh and stop as positive commands, and the controller exposes review as a required normal action. If match is restrictive, refresh, stop, review, and possibly install-and-run are denied. If match is not restrictive, the implementation still lacks an explicit verification that review is allowed.
issues.repair: Create a single canonical approved-action list containing exactly install-and-run, run, status, refresh, stop, and review. Generate match from that list, keep internal actions excluded, and run candidate and effective-policy positive checks over every listed action. Add a test that invokes the real policy checker for review and each other approved action, plus tests confirming internal actions remain denied.

residuals: The packet does not establish accounting correctness, scientific validity, or human acceptance; the reported test count is control-plane evidence only.
The packet does not provide the external execpolicy grammar, so the precise runtime consequence of the match mismatch remains dependent on that undocumented interface.
No additional hostile-worker, deliberate-detachment, or uncatchable-kill threat model is added beyond the stated containment scope.
next_actions: Repair the rule-generation and verification mismatch.
Rerun the permission-install tests with the real execpolicy checker, including review.
Record the exact policy semantics used by the implementation so future reviews can verify command coverage without inference.
